topik: MQTT Connectivity with MicroPython, Raspberry Pi Pico W, and Eclipse Mosquitto
tagline: Two boards exchange data through an Eclipse Mosquitto broker.
ringkasan: Two Raspberry Pi Pico W boards exchange data through an Eclipse Mosquitto broker running on an Orange Pi: one board publishes a potentiometer's position, and the other subscribes to the same topic and records every value that arrives.
Every group uses its own topic and mqtt_client_id, so many groups can share one broker without disturbing each other.

toolchain.label: Both Raspberry Pi Pico W boards (Publisher and Subscriber)

catatan: The Pico W's ADC input only tolerates up to 3.3 V, so the potentiometer's top leg must be fed from 3V3(OUT) (physical pin 36), not from the 5 V VBUS.
Its middle leg (the wiper) must land on one of the ADC pins, that is GP26, GP27 or GP28.

The Eclipse Mosquitto broker runs on the Orange Pi 4 PRO and needs no additional circuit. The Subscriber only records the values that arrive, so the second Pico W just needs to be on the same Wi-Fi network as the Publisher.

persiapan: Installing the mosquitto and mosquitto-clients packages on the Orange Pi (sudo apt install)
Enabling broker autostart: sudo systemctl enable mosquitto.service
Noting the Orange Pi's IP address with hostname -I
Editing /etc/mosquitto/mosquitto.conf, adding listener 1883 and allow_anonymous true
Restarting the service: sudo systemctl restart mosquitto.service
Installing the micropython-umqtt.simple library on both Pico W boards through Thonny
Powering the potentiometer from 3V3(OUT), not VBUS, and wiring its wiper to GP26
